title: Gluing derived complexes and compatible morphisms on two opens
statement: Let (X,\mathcal O_X) be a ringed space [def-pc-derived-category] with X=U\cup V. Given A\in D(\mathcal O_U), B\in D(\mathcal O_V), and an isomorphism c:A|_{U\cap V}\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_{U\cap V}, there is F\in D(\mathcal O_X) restricting to A and B with transition c. Given E\in D(\mathcal O_X) and compatible maps a:A\to E|_U and b:B\to E|_V (a|_{U\cap V}=b|_{U\cap V}\circ c), there is a map F\to E restricting to a and b.

proof.text: Let j_U, j_V, j_W be the open immersions of U, V and W=U\cap V into X, with derived direct images Rj_{U,*}, Rj_{V,*}, Rj_{W,*} as in [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. Form the morphism Rj_{U,*}A\oplus Rj_{V,*}B\to Rj_{W,*}(B|_W) whose V component is the restriction map and whose U component is the restriction map Rj_{U,*}A\to Rj_{W,*}(A|_W) followed by Rj_{W,*}c. By the triangulated structure of the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] (applied to the abelian category of \mathcal O_X-modules) it sits in a distinguished triangle F\to Rj_{U,*}A\oplus Rj_{V,*}B\to Rj_{W,*}(B|_W)\to F[1]; this defines F.

Restrict the triangle to U. By [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] (Tag 08FE) applied to f=j_V and the open U (so f^{-1}U=W and g=j:W\to U), to f=j_W and U (g=j), and to f=j_U and U (g=\mathrm{id}_U), the restriction to U of the V pushforward and of the W pushforward are both canonically Rj_*(B|_W), and the restriction of the U pushforward is A. Under these identifications, the second arrow is the difference of the map induced by c and the identity on the pushforward from U∩V, so its projection to the second summand is an isomorphism and has a section. The cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for a morphism with such a section is isomorphic to the triangle with first term A; hence F|_U≅A. Restricting to V gives F|_V≅B by the same displayed split-cone calculation with the two summands interchanged. Under these identifications, the two component maps on U∩V are c and the identity, so the transition isomorphism is c.

Let f:F|_U→A and g:F|_V→B be the restriction isomorphisms from Step 2. The maps f^{-1} followed by a and g^{-1} followed by b are maps from F to E on U and V. On U∩V their two composites agree because f and g identify the transition with c and a|_{U∩V}=b|_{U∩V}∘c. Thus the compatible pair is the pair required by the Mayer–Vietoris step.

The Mayer–Vietoris exact sequence for derived Hom [lem-sc-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris], applied to F and the target E, lifts this compatible pair to a global morphism F to E. Its restrictions are the prescribed maps by construction.
